text: Some voices carry further than they should. The lantern is lit.
picture: The Storyteller stands alone in a murky, fog-filled hollow, ankle-deep in mist that swathes the ground. He holds a red, glass-paned lantern low by his side, casting a dim, reddish glow that illuminates the mist at his boots. Far behind him, on a distant hill, a single upstairs window of a lonely house glows yellow in the vast, dark landscape.

text: My daughter Lily is four. She sleeps with the baby monitor on.
picture: Lily sleeps peacefully on her side, curled under a blue duvet patterned with white stars, her fair hair messy on the pillow. The room is softly lit by a small plastic star-shaped night-light plugged into a socket on the wall. On the wooden bedside table, the baby monitor sits, its single small red light glowing steadily, illuminating the device's edge.

text: Last night, at twelve past three, it crackled.
picture: Extreme close-up on the baby monitor receiver on Mara's bedside table, its small screen dark but the red LED sound-level lights at its base are active and brightly lit against the black plastic. The edge of a sleeping figure (Mara) is visible beyond it in the extreme background, blurred and out of focus. The only light in the room is the glow from the red lights.

text: Lily was whispering. "I can't. Mummy will hear."
picture: Lily is awake in her bed, her small face tense and scared. She clutches the edge of her star-patterned duvet tightly under her chin, her eyes wide and fixed on something unseen beyond the camera, her lips slightly parted as if whispering. The star night-light casts faint, soft light, creating deep shadows across half her face. The baby monitor's red light is a small, steady point of color on the bedside table.
sound: a faint, whispered child's voice, "I can't. Mummy will hear."

picture: Mara is now wide awake, frozen in her bed. She lies on her side, her body rigid, her eyes wide and unblinking as she stares directly at the baby monitor receiver on her bedside table. Her hand clutches the edge of her own blanket. The room is dark except for the glow from the monitor's jumping red sound-level LEDs, which illuminate her terrified face in brief, rhythmic flashes.
sound: a low, hushed, unnaturally patient male voice

picture: A close-up on Mara's face, her expression shifting from terror to horrifying realization. Her mouth is slightly open, her eyes locked on the baby monitor just beyond the frame, her pupils reflecting the small red glow. She holds her breath, a single tear welling in one eye.
sound: the same patient voice, whispering clearly, "Mummy is asleep."

text: I ran. Her door was shut. Her night-light was off. I had left it on.
picture: Mara stands frozen at the end of a dark upstairs hallway. She wears her grey cardigan and dark pyjamas, one hand reaching out to rest on the closed doorknob of Lily's bedroom door. The hallway's single ceiling bulb flickers erratically, casting stuttering light and long, shifting shadows. No light escapes from under Lily's door.
sound: the rapid, panicked thud of a heartbeat

text: Lily was asleep, facing the wall. Nobody else.
picture: From the bedroom doorway, looking in. Lily lies on her bed facing the far wall, a small lump under the covers in her pale yellow star-patterned pyjamas. The night-light on a low table is dark and unplugged. The corners of the small room are deep black and empty. Grey pre-dawn light seeps faintly around the edges of a drawn curtain at the window.

text: I sat on her floor until dawn, the monitor in my lap.
picture: Mara sits slumped on the floor against Lily's wall, her back against it. Her knees are drawn up, and she holds the baby monitor receiver in her lap with both hands, her fingers loosely curled around it. Her head leans back against the wall, eyes open but heavy-lidded, face slack with exhaustion. Grey pre-dawn light and a faint fog bleed around the edges of the window beside her. Lily is asleep in her bed beside Mara, a small shape under the covers.

text: At twenty to five, it crackled again. Lily hadn't moved.
picture: A close insert shot of Mara's hands holding the baby monitor receiver in her lap. The device's casing is black plastic. In the top corner, a single small red LED glows steadily. Her hands are very still.

text: Then the voice came, so close it touched the microphone. "Mummy's awake now."
picture: Mara sits frozen on the floor, her body rigid, staring down at the receiver in her lap with wide, horrified eyes. Her mouth is slightly open. In the dark corner of the room just behind her left shoulder, a tall, impossibly thin shadow of a figure bends down from the wall. It is darker than the surrounding darkness, a silhouette with no discernible face or features, leaning its head toward Mara's ear as if to whisper. Lily remains asleep in her bed.

text: Lily is five now. She still won't sleep without the monitor. She says he likes to listen.
picture: The Storyteller stands alone in the rocky hollow. He has just lowered his red-paned lantern to his side, so its crimson glow now mostly lights the ground around his boots. His face is solemn and shadowed. Far behind him, high up and tiny in the distance, is the window of a house's upper floor. In the absolute center of that small dark window, a single, steady red point of light glows.
